I think your insufficiently-requited love is wrong about the ethics of offering the trade, provided you don't want to lie- but the other person won't actually be able to simulate you in enough detail that this should directly be an issue? Newcombe does strange things to my brain.

Is the implication at the end that not selling the vote (without disclosing the counterfactual) is equivalent to running CDT? Maybe because the question of whether to vote-trade is correlated with the decisions faced by other voters, and close enough that the fraction of voters runnning something like TDT is relevant?
